sessionTitle: Fabric IQ: Bringing enterprise intelligence into the developer workflow

announcements.name: Graph analytics in Fabric IQ is generally available
announcements.shortDescription: Native graph capabilities built on OneLake data and the ontology, with a visual no-code GQL query builder for multi-hop relationship and causal analysis without additional ETL
announcements.longDescription: Graph capabilities in Fabric IQ are generally available, taking the power of OneLake data and the ontology to power relationship and causal analysis. Using a visual no-code query builder, users can construct rich GQL queries without writing code, selecting nodes like entrances, course segments, and seating sections and filtering to get fast graph results. This enables understanding the implications of events at one entity (e.g., an entrance) on related areas such as a seating section, with results viewable in diagram or list views.

announcements.name: Operations Agent generally available in Fabric IQ
announcements.shortDescription: An agent that monitors anomaly events, Eventhouse data, and the ontology in real time, then recommends and takes governed actions, operating within a team channel
announcements.longDescription: The Operations Agent in Fabric IQ is generally available, demonstrated as part of showing how AI works with ontologies. It is grounded on the real business context represented in the ontology and powered by real-time intelligence, integrating with Microsoft Foundry, Microsoft Copilot Studio, and out-of-the-box Fabric agents. The demo shows pairing it with an anomaly detector over Eventhouse data that uses data science to recommend the best model and emit anomaly events automatically as data streams in.

announcements.name: Business events in the real-time hub
announcements.shortDescription: Ability to publish curated business events from notebooks for anyone in Fabric to subscribe to for analytics or action
announcements.longDescription: Business events are now available directly in the real-time hub, providing the ability to publish curated business events for anyone within Fabric to subscribe to, whether for analytics or action purposes. This was among the real-time intelligence updates released leading up to Build and was shown in the demo.

announcements.name: Geospatial map visualization generally available in Fabric
announcements.shortDescription: Map item for real-time and analytical geospatial needs
announcements.longDescription: Geospatial visualization in the map item directly within Fabric is generally available, ready for all geospatial needs across both real-time and analytical scenarios. It can be used alongside all of the other pieces across Fabric. This was the final item in a whirlwind tour of real-time intelligence capabilities.

announcements.name: Real-time intelligence updates leading into Build
announcements.shortDescription: GA of the SQL operator in Eventstream, Spark Structured Streaming support with Eventstream, DeltaFlow for event-driven apps, Copilot in real-time intelligence, and MCP plus skills
announcements.longDescription: A set of real-time intelligence updates were released leading up to Build, including the GA of the SQL operator in Eventstream for expressing custom business logic using SQL, and support for Spark Structured Streaming with Eventstream to stream process using Python via a connection between Eventstream and Spark Notebooks. New capabilities for event-driven applications with DeltaFlow make it easy to transform Debezium [inferred] feeds into analytics-ready events without customizing the Eventstream directly. Additional updates include Copilot capabilities in real-time intelligence and a set of MCP and skills to bring real-time data to agents.

announcements.name: Anomaly detector in public preview
announcements.shortDescription: Recommends the best model to detect anomalies on streaming Eventhouse data and emits anomaly events automatically
announcements.longDescription: The anomaly detector capability is in public preview, making it easy to connect to existing Eventhouse data. It leverages data science to analyze data patterns and recommend the best model to detect anomalies, emitting anomaly detector events automatically when conditions are met. This was described alongside other out-of-box capabilities including building a RAG solution with Eventhouse, the generally available Data agent, and the Operations Agent in Fabric IQ.

announcements.name: Physical AI preview with NVIDIA
announcements.shortDescription: Real-time dashboards using OpenUSD scenes integrated with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries for bidirectional 3D operational visualization
announcements.longDescription: Through a strategic partnership with NVIDIA, a physical AI solution is in preview that connects streams of data and embeds them in a real-time dashboard using OpenUSD scenes integrated with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. This creates a 3D visualization showing in real time how systems operate, with bidirectional cross-highlight capabilities for a unified operational picture. It combines Fabric real-time intelligence to collect signals, Fabric IQ and the ontology studio for contextualized visuals, and NVIDIA Omniverse for 3D visualization and physical simulation, enabling operations across both digital and physical worlds.

announcements.name: Planning in Fabric IQ
announcements.shortDescription: Announced at FABCON; enables what-if scenarios over trusted data for business and finance teams
announcements.longDescription: Planning in Fabric IQ, announced at FABCON, allows you to plan, understand, and run what-if scenarios over the same trusted data. This makes it powerful for enabling business and finance teams. It was presented as part of an overview of Fabric IQ capabilities alongside the graph analytics multi-hop analysis.
